 For Respondent-5,8 and13 : Not Ready in Notice  ORDER The Writ of Mandamus has been instituted to direct the respondents 1 to 9 to take appropriate action against the tenth respondent for selling unlicensed medicines to the petitioner. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2 . The learned counsel for the petitioner Mr.S.Ilamvaludhi would state that the petitioner purchased the Shampoo called 'Swadeshi Herbal Shampoo' on 21.11.2018 at 'Swadeshi Mandir', No.61,
Wallajah Road, Anna Salai, Chennai-600 002 and the shop owner compelled the petitioner to purchase another medicines called 'Aloevera Extract', 'Amla Powder', 'Sarvarog Nashak Churna',
'Vibhuti (Bhasm)' and 'Triphala Powder'.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would further state that after using the said Shampoo viz.,
Swadeshi Herbal Shampoo, the petitioner found that she suffered with hair fall and the advertisement made by the tenth respondent regarding the said powder viz., 'Sarvarog Nashak Churna' are completely misleading and false. Such advertisements given by the manufacturers or the retailers for selling such products misleading the public at large would attract the provisions under Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 [hereinafter referred to as the 'Act', in short]. Any false or misleading advertisements of drugs or other products are made,
then the Authorities Competent are bound to invoke the provisions of the Act and prosecute the persons in the manner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis contemplated. 
4. In the present case, the grievance of the petitioner is that the complaint given by her was not investigated properly by the authorities. 
Thus the petitioner is constrained to move the present writ petition. 
5. Pertinently, the official respondents have not filed any counter-affidavit in the present writ petition, despite the fact that the present writ petition is pending for the past about four years. The inaction and omission on the part of the official respondents in dealing with such serious matters are to be deprecated. The Drugs Inspector, Triplicane one Smt.S.Dhanalakshmi,
W/o.Mr.C.Seenivasan filed a Report before this Court in the present writ petition stating that the H.Kanchana Hariharan vs The Secretary To Government on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119110607/
4 product 'Sarvarog Nashak Churna' as stated by the petitioner that the label of the product claims to cure certain diseases, which will attract Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements)
Act, 1954. After inspection of the premises of the tenth respondent and on enquiry, the tenth respondent stated that the said product is a food supplement and he is holding a food license to manufacture the product. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6. The Drugs Inspector merely accepting the statement of the tenth respondent is unacceptable and the Drugs Inspector was very much knowing about the advertisements given by the tenth respondent visibly on the product and in the label. In such circumstances, the Drugs Inspector with reference to the advertisements has to take samples and sent it for laboratory test, identify the character and nature of the products and if any illegality or wrongful information is provided, then prosecute the persons under the relevant Statutes. 
7. The Report submitted by Smt.S.Dhanalakshmi, the Drugs Inspector would indicate that she had failed to perform her duties as required under law. Therefore, the Director of Drugs Control has to conduct an enquiry and initiate appropriate actions against the said Drugs Inspector, namely,
Smt.S.Dhanalakshmi, if she had failed to do her duties in initiating appropriate actions against such misleading advertisements or lapses, negligence or dereliction of duty. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8. In view of the facts and circumstances, this Court has no other option, but to direct the respondents 1 to 9 to depute an Officer not below the rank of Assistant Director of Drugs Control to conduct an inspection in the tenth respondent shop premises, test the products and the advertisements given and initiate all appropriate actions in the manner known to law if any illegalities are identified. The said enquiry or action to be initiated by the Authorities are directed to be monitored by the fourth respondent-Director of Drugs Control. The abovesaid exercise is directed to be completed by the respondents 1 to 9, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order. 
9. With the above directions, the present writ petition stands allowed. However, there shall be no order as to costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.

summary.arguments:
Any false or misleading advertisements of drugs or other products are made,
then the Authorities Competent are bound to invoke the provisions of the Act and prosecute the persons in the manner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis contemplated.
summary.facts:
Thus the petitioner is constrained to move the present writ petition.
The Drugs Inspector merely accepting the statement of the tenth respondent is unacceptable and the Drugs Inspector was very much knowing about the advertisements given by the tenth respondent visibly on the product and in the label.
In such circumstances, the Drugs Inspector with reference to the advertisements has to take samples and sent it for laboratory test, identify the character and nature of the products and if any illegality or wrongful information is provided, then prosecute the persons under the relevant Statutes.
7. The Report submitted by Smt.S.Dhanalakshmi, the Drugs Inspector would indicate that she had failed to perform her duties as required under law.
Therefore, the Director of Drugs Control has to conduct an enquiry and initiate appropriate actions against the said Drugs Inspector, namely,
Smt.S.Dhanalakshmi, if she had failed to do her duties in initiating appropriate actions against such misleading advertisements or lapses, negligence or dereliction of duty.
summary.ANALYSIS:
5. Pertinently, the official respondents have not filed any counter-affidavit in the present writ petition, despite the fact that the present writ petition is pending for the past about four years.
The inaction and omission on the part of the official respondents in dealing with such serious matters are to be deprecated.
summary.decision:
In view of the facts and circumstances, this Court has no other option, but to direct the respondents 1 to 9 to depute an Officer not below the rank of Assistant Director of Drugs Control to conduct an inspection in the tenth respondent shop premises, test the products and the advertisements given and initiate all appropriate actions in the manner known to law if any illegalities are identified.
The said enquiry or action to be initiated by the Authorities are directed to be monitored by the fourth respondent-Director of Drugs Control.
The abovesaid exercise is directed to be completed by the respondents 1 to 9, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
9. With the above directions, the present writ petition stands allowed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
